description:
## What breaks

Two expressions written next to each other on one line parse, and everything after the first is dropped without a diagnostic.

```
fn main() do
  a = 1 2
  dbg(a)
end
```

prints `1`. So does `a = "p" "q"` -- it prints `"p"`. Elixir rejects both as syntax errors.

## Why it matters

This is the mechanism behind the heredoc failure. `"""` is three quote characters, which lex as an empty string followed by another string, so `a = """ ... """` is a juxtaposition and `a` silently becomes `""`. Fixing heredoc lexing removes that particular spelling, but any typo that lands two expressions on one line still compiles to something the author did not write.

A parser that accepts a sequence of expressions where one is expected cannot tell the reader they made a mistake, and the value it picks -- the first -- is not obviously more correct than any other choice.

## Acceptance

- `a = 1 2` is a diagnostic naming the unexpected second expression, on every door.
- Legitimate juxtapositions stay legal: a `do` block on the same line, keyword arguments, `fn (x) -> x end` inline, and whatever else the suite already proves.
- The fixture suite passes unchanged, or every change is a program that was silently wrong.
title: [BUG] Juxtaposed expressions on one line are accepted and all but the first discarded
